topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and core learning objectives for the lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional modalities for treating cancer—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated toxicities and drug resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Targeting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities and defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies designed to exploit specific biological defects in cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependence, cell cycle checkpoint failure, and DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the rationale of targeting oncogene addiction with small-molecule kinase inhibitors and the molecular mechanisms that drive drug resistance and bypass pathways.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody therapies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the design and therapeutic applications of monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates directed against tumor cell surface antigens.

topics.label: Immune surveillance and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for natural immune surveillance and contemporary strategies to reactivate or engineer T cells to eliminate tumor cells.

topics.label: Overarching challenges, historical perspectives, and future directions in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader clinical challenges in cancer management, historical trends in mortality and prevention, and future therapeutic and ethical paradigms.
